refuted.fact: editorial_brief / corrections_to_candidate_list item 4: 'the two posts cross-link each other'.
refuted.why: One-way only. The developer post's first sentence links the words 'new Gemini Live models' to the model post. The model post contains no link to the developer post: grep for the developer slug in the model post HTML returns zero hits, and an enumeration of every href in the model post body yields only ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/live-api, cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-cx, the model card, deepmind.google/models/synthid/ and six partner doc sites. The one-article decision still stands, but on the identical RSS pubDate (which I confirmed), not on mutual linking.

refuted.fact: not_said item 12: 'the Live API thinking guide describes upgrading from [gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview] as an optional migration.'
refuted.why: The guide never says optional. Its section is titled 'Migration and integration paths' -> 'Upgrading from Gemini 3.1 Flash Live' and gives concrete upgrade steps. Searching that page for 'optional' and 'deprecat' returns only the sidebar nav item 'Deprecations'. The underlying point (no deprecation notice for gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview on the pricing page, the Live API page or the thinking guide) is correct; the characterisation is invented.

refuted.fact: must_not_write item 6: 'Do not say Gemini 3.8 Live is in the Gemini app. Google's launch post puts 3.8 Live in Search Live and Extended Thinking in Gemini Live.'
refuted.why: This tells the writer to suppress a first-party statement. The DeepMind model card, which Google links from its own launch post, reads: 'Gemini 3.8 Live is distributed in the following channels: Gemini API, Gemini App, Google AI Studio, Google Cloud / Vertex AI, Google Search Live.' The launch post's own prose also says the models make speaking with Gemini 'across the Gemini app, Google Workspace, and Search' more fluid (the researcher records this as fact 21). The instruction also contradicts the researcher's own unverified_or_excluded item 3, which correctly says 'Flag the discrepancy rather than resolving it'. Rewrite to: report the blog's consumer split, and say Google's model card lists a wider channel set including the Gemini app and Vertex AI.

unsupported.fact: verified_fact 8: "Google frames the pair as 'our most advanced live dialogue models yet' (meta description and standfirst)", with quote ending 'built for natural conversation.'
unsupported.why: That sentence exists only in <meta name=description> and og:description. The visible standfirst reads '...are our most advanced live dialogue models yet. Major upgrades in intelligence and parallel reasoning make them more intuitive to collaborate with and use to execute complex tasks using your voice.' The phrase 'built for natural conversation' appears nowhere in the article body. The 'and standfirst' attribution is wrong; the rest of the fact holds.

unsupported.fact: event_date_basis: 'A fourth corroboration is the Gemini API pricing page footer, Last updated 2026-09-15 UTC.'
unsupported.why: That footer is a site-wide docs build stamp, not an event date. I found the identical string 'Last updated 2026-09-15 UTC.' on ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/live-api, a page that never mentions gemini-3.8-live. It corroborates only that the docs set was rebuilt that day. The three genuine confirmations (two meta published_time values, two identical RSS pubDates, model card 'Published 15 September 2026') are enough; drop the fourth.

unsupported.fact: corrections_to_candidate_list item 3 as framed: Google's own Live API overview doc 'still said Converse in 70 supported languages', offered as a check on the 97 figure.
unsupported.why: Both halves of the observation are true and I reproduced them (the string is there; '97' is absent from the page), but the page is a platform-level Live API feature list that never names gemini-3.8-live or any model, and its own footer also reads 'Last updated 2026-09-15 UTC'. Report it as three separate figures from three Google pages (97 in the launch post, 97+ in the developer post, 70 on the Live API overview page on the day we checked) and do not let the article imply Google's docs deny 97 for these models.

additional_findings: MISSED FIRST-PARTY SOURCE, material. The model card's Evaluation section links 'Evals & Methodology for 3.8 Live Extended Thinking' -> https://deepmind.google/models/evals-methodology/gemini-3-8-live, which redirects (HTTP 200) to https://storage.googleapis.com/deepmind-media/gemini/gemini_3-8_live_model_evaluation.pdf, a 5-page Google DeepMind PDF titled 'Gemini 3.8 Audio (Live, Live Extended Thinking) Model evaluation'. The researcher never fetched it. It qualifies every benchmark claim in the article: 'All Gemini scores are pass@1 except where otherwise noted'; 'ServiceNow's EVA-Bench results were run by ServiceNow with the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (thinking minimal and high)'; 'Artificial Analysis (run by AA) and tau-Bench results were run with the Gemini API for the model-ids gemini-3.8-live-preview and gemini-3.8-live-extended-thinking with thinking high and default sampling settings'; results are 'as of September 2026'.

The eval PDF names the benchmarked model-id as gemini-3.8-live-preview, which is NOT the identifier printed on the pricing page (gemini-3.8-live). Google's own documents use two ids for the same model. If the article prints an id, use the pricing page's, and do not present the scores as measured on the generally available model without that caveat.

The score charts inside the eval PDF are images: 82.6, 68.6%, 35.1% and 97.7% are not extractable as text from it. Those four numbers are traceable only to the blog post, which makes the 'Google 表示' attribution in must_not_write mandatory rather than stylistic.

Google names the Sierra benchmark two different ways in its own material: the blog post's raw markup reads '68.6% on tau-Voice and 35.1% on Sierra's tau-Voice-banking benchmark', while the eval PDF calls it 'Sierra tau-cubed-Bench (tau-cubed-Banking)'. Quote the blog wording verbatim; do not merge or silently correct the names.

MATERIAL OMISSION from verified_facts: two figure captions in the model post carry Google's official surface names, which the availability table should use. 'Try Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking in Google Workspace with Docs Live, Gmail Live, and Keep Live.' and 'Get step-by-step, real-time troubleshooting help powered by Gemini 3.8 Live - right inside Search Live.' They independently confirm the model split and are the only place Google names Docs Live / Gmail Live / Keep Live.

MATERIAL OMISSION: the section head 'Across Google Workspace and Search, our Live models deliver more intuitive, collaborative experiences - especially when tackling your most complex tasks' is a third, looser surface statement on the same page and is absent from the record.

The model card lists 'Google Cloud / Vertex AI' as a distribution channel for BOTH models, while the blog post's availability list never mentions Vertex AI at all. This is captured inside verified_fact 22 but dropped from the proposed 4x5 availability table and from the 2x2 diagram, whose enterprise node says only 'Gemini Enterprise 私人預覽'. The enterprise picture is Gemini Enterprise private preview AND Vertex AI.

BETTER FIRST-PARTY SOURCE for the 3.5 Transcribe date, which the record leaves at 'released last month': Google's own launch post, linked from the model post's Related stories, is https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/gemini-models/gemini-3-5-transcribe/ with meta article:published_time 2026-08-26 and <title> 'Introducing Gemini 3.5 Transcribe'.

The Live API thinking guide (HTTP 200) documents the mechanism behind the headline 'background tool execution' claim and the hard split between the two models: thinking_level is not supported for gemini-3.8-live; gemini-3.8-live-extended-thinking takes thinking_level low/medium/high with MINIMAL not supported; Extended Thinking 'Requires asynchronous (NON_BLOCKING) tool declarations' and callers must track interaction_status instead of turnComplete. Keeping it out of sources to respect the 4-source cap is defensible, but this is the substance of the claim the article is built on.

I checked one further obvious first-party channel for the missing region and eligibility scope: the Google Workspace Updates blog Atom feed (HTTP 200, 25 entries, newest 2026-09-16). Its 2026-09-15 entries cover Meet room codes, Gemini connectors, Gmail Search AI Overviews and Drive sharing - nothing on Docs Live / Gmail Live / Keep Live or 3.8 Live Extended Thinking. This corroborates the record's 'no region scope published' finding rather than contradicting it.
